To add on to your post, mineral water is better than tap water for the same reason.

Pure water is 7.0 on the Ph scale. Tap water is probably around 7.3-7.8 depending on various things.

Natural mineral filled water (like what you'd get from a stream in the mountains or a lake) is in the 8.2-8.8 Ph range.

Remember that the Ph scale is a relative scale from 0-14 where 0 is pure acidic and 14 is pure alkaline. 11 is acidic relative to 12 but alkaline overall.

So, tap water or water that has been distilled/purified is acidic to your mouth, when compared to mineral water.

Another thing is that over brushing is a thing. Brush too hard and/or for too long and you are doing more damage to your teeth than the acid from the bacteria is.

After having a particularly acidic meal (i.e. soda and lots of sugar or otherwise), you should probably wash your mouth out and wait some time before brushing.
